los.text: Demonstrate a systematic examination of the gastrointestinal system
los.html:
1. IntroductionWash hands, introduce, consent, position flat with one pillow, expose nipples to knees (keep covered except the abdomen), ask about pain.
2. General inspectionJaundice, pallor, cachexia, distension, scars, stomas, around the bed.
3. HandsClubbing, koilonychia, leuconychia, palmar erythema, Dupuytren's, asterixis (liver flap).
4. ArmsBruising, scratch marks, fistulas.
5. FaceConjunctival pallor, scleral icterus, angular cheilitis, mouth ulcers, xanthelasma.
6. NeckLymph nodes, especially Virchow's (left supraclavicular).
7. ChestSpider naevi, gynaecomastia.
8. Abdomen inspectionScars, distension, caput medusae, visible peristalsis; ask to cough (hernias).
9. PalpateLight then deep (nine regions), then liver, spleen (from the right iliac fossa), kidneys (ballot), aorta.
10. PercussLiver, spleen, shifting dullness.
11. AuscultateBowel sounds, renal and aortic bruits.
12. FinishHernial orifices, external genitalia, DRE, urine dip, observations; thank the patient and present.

los.text: Organise and present clinical findings in a structured and logical format
los.html:
OrderOpening statement (who, what you examined), positive findings, relevant negatives, then summary and differential.
Example
  • "On examination of Mrs X's abdomen, she appeared comfortable at rest.
  • There were no peripheral stigmata of chronic liver disease.
  • The abdomen was soft with tenderness in the right upper quadrant and a positive Murphy's sign.
  • There was no organomegaly or shifting dullness.
  • In summary… The most likely diagnosis is acute cholecystitis."
TipsStand up straight, look at the examiner, avoid "um", commit to a most likely diagnosis.

los.text: Conduct a focused history for a patient presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms
los.html:
AreaQuestions
PainSOCRATES
Upper GIDysphagia, odynophagia, reflux, nausea, vomiting (haematemesis, coffee grounds), early satiety
Lower GIBowel habit change, diarrhoea, constipation, blood (fresh, mixed, melaena), mucus, tenesmus
LiverJaundice, pale stools, dark urine, itch
GeneralWeight loss, appetite, fever, night sweats
Red flagsDysphagia, GI bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, mass, age >55 with new symptoms
Risk factorsAlcohol, NSAIDs, family history of bowel cancer/IBD, travel, contacts

los.text: Explore and evaluate a patient’s experience of pain using effective communication techniques
los.html:
SOCRATESQuestion
SiteWhere is it? Point to it.
OnsetWhen did it start? Sudden or gradual?
CharacterSharp, dull, burning, colicky?
RadiationDoes it go anywhere else?
AssociationsNausea, vomiting, fever, jaundice?
Time courseConstant or comes and goes? Getting worse?
Exacerbating / relieving factorsFood, movement, position, painkillers?
SeverityOut of 10; effect on sleep and activity
  • Explore the impact: "How is the pain affecting you day to day?", and their ideas and concerns about it.

los.text: Summarise the patient’s account to confirm mutual understanding during consultation
los.html:
SummarisingPeriodically restate the key points in your own words: "So, just to check I've understood…"
Then"Have I missed anything?" (lets the patient correct or add).
Benefit
Confirms accuracy
Shows you've listened
Organises your thinking
Gives a natural transition between sections
